note: Package A: gates on the speed runs (ci/speed-compare.py). Each default-on approximation keeps removing work and doesn't make frames slower, in the scenes where it was measured to help. Options (off by default) are reported, not gated. approx.fog-sections measured in full run 45310672623 (on/off, median of the rounds' own ratios): spawn triangles 0.927 / 0.920, frame ms 0.920 / 0.928, 31.5 sections in fog a frame; fly-through 19-26 sections a frame. Package B: the fog-sections auto-off check (ci.fog-unconfirmed), translucent terrain by region (approx.translucent-regions), and fog-sections in the nether's environmental fog.

gates.reason: the render-distance fog test must still find sections to leave out at spawn (31.5 a frame when measured)
leaving those sections out must cut terrain triangles (0.92-0.93 when measured; 0.96 leaves room for the camera's pose)
it must not make frames slower (0.92-0.93 when measured)
the moving fly-through must also find fogged sections (19-26 a frame when measured)
with the fog end unconfirmed (as with a mod that replaces vanilla's fog code), fog-sections must switch itself off and leave nothing out
translucent terrain drawn region by region must cut draw calls on the plain path (old GPU)
and must not make frames slower (3% for the moving fly-through's noise)
package B: the nether's environmental fog (it ends at about half the render distance) must let fog-sections leave sections out above and below the eye (113 a frame when measured)

and must cut the terrain drawn (0.60-0.62 when measured). Not gated on frame time here: on CI occlusion already hides most fogged nether sections, so frame time moves by noise only (full run 45369287133, speed-old rounds 1.084 / 0.963 / 1.046)
